description: A rename (BATCH_WINDOW -> BATCH_WINDOW_SECONDS) migrated metrics.py but left producer.py and consumer.py importing and using the old name: ImportError at import time in both. This is the shape ADR-0013's `group` exists for — ONE defect that a Finding cannot express, because a finding names one path and one line (ADR-0009's addendum C), so the reviewer has to file two and SAY they are one fix. Both defective lines are inside diff hunks (the PR adds a docstring above each), so both are anchorable and neither can be demoted to residual_risk: the question that decides is 'could I confirm it?', and an ImportError from a name that demonstrably no longer exists is confirmed. metrics.py is the control — it was migrated correctly, so a finding against it is a false positive.
grouping_note: Both caller findings are required and every finding on those paths must share one group. A finding on the removed constant declaration may optionally join them when its exact location and BATCH_WINDOW diagnosis match optional_grouped_findings. If reported, that root-cause finding must share the callers' group. Its absence is fine; it cannot replace a caller or bridge split caller groups. Other findings, including unrelated changes on constants.py, cannot collapse into this group. This replaces the former under-grouping workaround without requiring a third finding.
line_accuracy_note: Exact line 8 in both files: `deadline = clock() + BATCH_WINDOW` and `since = clock() - BATCH_WINDOW`. The import on line 1 of each file is NOT in a hunk (the diff's window starts at 4), so anchoring to the import rejects on provenance — which is correct and is why the use site is the anchor. The two files' hunks are identical in shape, so a file-attribution slip lands on a coincidentally-valid line in the other file and only the two findings_any entries catch it.
max_findings_note: The ceiling stays at 3. Two required callers leave room for either the optional root-cause finding or one separate test-coverage note. Optional group membership does not increase the output budget.
